subject: Post-call: latency guardrails, burst provisioning, and quantization path
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Park <lisa.park@zenosys.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: latency guardrails, burst provisioning, and quantization path

Hi Lisa — thanks for the time today. High-level recap and agreed next steps from our side: 

TL;DR
- Primary customer goals: p99 inference <= 200ms for conversational scoring; maintain quality within ~5% of current model; target cost reduction via caching/quantization.
- Primary constraints: spiky traffic (bursts up to 3x baseline for 10-15m), strict data residency (US-west), procurement timeline in ~6 weeks.

What we heard (pain points)
- Current vendor shows p99 ~340ms under production traffic; KV cache miss rate ~18% during peaks.
- SLO is business-critical for live agent handoff; anything above 250ms materially impacts conversions.
- They have a hard procurement window and need a deployment plan + cost estimate to move forward.

Proposed topology (recap)
- Primary: Redwood Dedicated pool in us-west (4 active GPUs, autoscale to 8 for burst windows).
- Fallback: Cross-region warm standby (us-east) for regional failover (cold-start acceptable for <5% traffic).
- Caching: prefix + KV cache with a warming strategy; aim to reduce miss rate to <5% for steady-state.
- Model: 8-bit quantized candidate for inference, with an eval plan to validate quality delta <=5%.

Immediate next steps (action owners)
1) Share topology sketch and initial cost delta — Michael (attached: deployment-topology-v1.pdf).
2) Zeno to share 72-hr traffic snapshot + representative prompt set — Lisa.
3) Redwood infra deep-dive (batching/kv/cache/kernel selection) — Karthik to prepare a short sim and sizing notes.
4) Schedule 60m tech deep-dive next week to align on acceptance criteria and test harness.

Can you confirm the traffic snapshot and preferred time for the deep-dive? If possible, please attach the 72-hr export (CSV) and one canonical prompt per flow so we can run an apples-to-apples eval.

Thanks again — we’ll stand up the simulation after the snapshot and follow up with a formal MMP (mutual action plan).

Best,
Michael Grant
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[m] +1 (415) 555-0176

From: Lisa Park <lisa.park@zenosys.com>

Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency guardrails, burst provisioning, and quantization path

Thanks Michael — great summary. A few clarifications and attachments below.

Confirmations/clarifications:
- p99 target: 200ms hard internal goal, 250ms upper bound for public-facing scoring.
- Quality tolerance: up to 5% relative metric (we typically use Rouge-L / top-choice accuracy for our scoring tasks).
- Burst profile: we see 2.5-3.2x spikes lasting between 8-18m, generally tied to batch job windows on the upstream pipeline.

Attached: prod_traffic_snapshot.csv (72h export) and a short prompt_sample.txt (one canonical prompt per scoring flow).

Procurement note: cc’ing our procurement lead (procurement@zenosys.com) on the thread — they’ll need a high-level SoW and lead time estimate to start internal approvals.

Available times for the deep-dive: Mon 11/09 10:00-12:00 PT or Tue 11/10 14:00-16:00 PT. Prefer the 90m slot so we can walk through test harness and acceptance criteria.

Lisa Park
Head of ML Engineering, Zeno Systems
lisa.park@zenosys.com | +1 (415) 777-2233
[attachment: prod_traffic_snapshot.csv (CSV, 120KB)]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 18:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency guardrails, burst provisioning, and quantization path

Noted. I’ll run a quick batching + KV cache simulation against their 72h snapshot once Lisa confirms the CSV link. Preliminary thoughts:
- Start sims on a 4-GPU A100-equivalent pool with dynamic batching (max batch window 25ms) and an autoscale policy to 8 GPUs for sustained peak >2x baseline.
- Test 8-bit and 4-bit quantized variants for throughput; measure top-choice accuracy on Lisa’s prompt sample.
- Kernel selection: likely use grouped GEMM path for long sequences, fused-attn for shorter conversational snippets — I’ll document expected kernel choices in the sim notes.

I’ll drop a short doc to the shared drive and flag items that need engineering time.

— Karthik
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>

- Confirmed meeting time: Mon 11/09 10:30 PT (we agreed to the 90m slot; calendar invite to follow).
- Owners: 
  * Topology + cost delta doc — Michael (deliverable: 11/08 COB).
  * Sizing sims + kernel selection notes — Karthik (deliverable: 11/10 EOD).

I’ve uploaded the initial topology sketch and a tracking sheet to the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_topology — please add your simulation artifacts there. We’ll iterate after the deep-dive and produce an MMP for procurement.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
